title: In Search of a Hero
bookshelves: Category: Biography, Literature and Literary studies
summary: In Search of a Hero: Tragic Irony in Graham Greene’s Fiction by Yuliya Kazanova offers a fresh perspective on Graham Greene, resituating his work within the European intellectual landscape of the twentieth century. While Greene remains best known for his Catholic novels and cinematic thrillers, this volume also highlights his lesser-known but still significant works. In doing so, it reveals Greene to be a far more complex and intellectually adventurous writer than is often acknowledged. By examining his suppressed novels of the 1930s and 1960s, alongside his plays, film scripts, and overlooked fiction, In Search of a Hero shows how Greene’s work responds powerfully and consistently to the twentieth century’s crisis of humanism. It illuminates the depth of his engagement with a broad range of intellectual influences—Freudian and Jungian psychoanalysis, Marxist social critique, Catholic theology, existentialist philosophy, as well as literary modernism and postmodernism. These influences actively shape the moral ambiguities, narrative experiments, and psychological tensions that define Greene’s writing. This reflects his response to the moral and spiritual crises of the twentieth century, and reveal his concern with ethical ambiguity and human fragility. Greene’s tragic irony captures his vision of human condition, in which an everyman makes a fraught existential choice and becomes a flawed tragic hero who opposes an overpowering force – be it moral evil, religious dogma or political ideology. In Search of a Hero redefines Greene’s legacy, demonstrating why his writing remains vital to the English novel of the 20th century.
